editorial.headline: Heating and Geothermal Installation, With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 43222 covers the building systems work that makes heating, geothermal and thermal protection function as one installed whole.
editorial.body:
KBLI 43222 concerns the installation and maintenance of heating and geothermal equipment in residential and non-residential buildings, whether electrical or non-electrical. In practice, it is a building-services activity with a wide technical perimeter: pipework, ducting and sheet-metal work; central-heating controls; connections to district heating; domestic boilers and burners; masonry heating furnaces; and solar-thermal collectors all sit within its stated scope. So do the less visible systems that determine whether a thermal installation performs safely over time: insulation for pipes and tanks, weatherproof external wall insulation, insulation for hot- and cold-water pipes, steam boilers and exhaust ducts, fire-resistant insulation, and fire-protection systems.

That breadth matters because the activity is not defined by a single appliance or energy source. It is the work of putting together—and maintaining—the heating, geothermal, distribution, control and protective elements required within a building. The code is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, making it relevant from smaller specialist installation businesses through to larger building-services operations. Its scope also expressly includes both homes and non-residential premises, so the dividing line is the character of the installation work, not the building’s use alone.

Nationally, the position is straightforward: the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. For a foreign investor, that means the national ownership setting does not impose a foreign-stake cap below full ownership for this activity.

Bali requires the same plain reading of the record rather than a borrowed assumption. This activity is not blocked for PMA registration by the provincial moratorium. The specific Bali assessment is that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; accordingly, it is not caught by that moratorium. The Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. In other words, the national openness remains meaningful in Bali for this code, while the applicable risk position at the large-business scale should be read as part of the activity’s local registration context.
